record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Model theory of deeply ramified fields
record.original_question: What model-theoretic statements can be proved for (roughly) deeply ramified valued fields relative to their value groups and residue fields? In particular, what can be said about the model theory of the perfect hull F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}, which is discussed as a central example of a deeply ramified field that remains outside the existing tame and roughly tame transfer results?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(K,v)$ be a valued field with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_K$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}_K$, value group $vK$, and residue field $Kv = \mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{m}_K$. Recall:

- $(K,v)$ is henselian if $v$ extends uniquely to every algebraic extension of $K$.
- $(K,v)$ is tame if it is henselian, $Kv$ is perfect, $vK/p\,vK = 0$ when $\operatorname{char}(Kv)=p>0$, and every finite extension is defectless.
- $(K,v)$ of residue characteristic $p>0$ is deeply ramified if $\Omega^1_{\mathcal{O}_L/\mathcal{O}_K} = 0$ for every finite extension $L/K$; equivalently (in the henselian case of characteristic $p$) the Frobenius $\Phi:\mathcal{O}_K/p\mathcal{O}_K \to \mathcal{O}_K/p\mathcal{O}_K$ is surjective and the field is dense in its perfect hull.

A standard transfer (Ax–Kochen/Ershov) principle for a class $\mathcal{C}$ of valued fields states: for $(K_1,v_1),(K_2,v_2)\in\mathcal{C}$,
$$ (K_1,v_1)\equiv (K_2,v_2) \iff v_1K_1 \equiv v_2K_2 \text{ (as ordered abelian groups) and } K_1v_1 \equiv K_2v_2 \text{ (as fields)},$$
with an analogous principle for elementary substructures.

Problem. Develop the model theory of (roughly) deeply ramified valued fields relative to their value groups and residue fields. Specifically:

(a) Formulate and prove an Ax–Kochen/Ershov style transfer principle (for elementary equivalence and for elementary substructure) for a natural class of deeply ramified valued fields that strictly contains the class of (roughly) tame valued fields and that is not covered by existing tame or roughly tame transfer results.

(b) Determine a complete set of axioms, in a suitable first-order language of valued fields, for the theory of the perfect hull
$$ \mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)^{1/p^{\infty}} = \bigcup_{n\ge 0} \mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)^{1/p^n} $$
equipped with its $t$-adic valuation, and decide its decidability, model-completeness, NIP, and the structure of its definable sets, relative to its value group $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$ and residue field $\mathbb{F}_p$.
artifact.status_search_result: Jahnke and Kartas (Beyond the Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem, JAMS 2025) established AKE-type principles for certain perfect deeply ramified / perfectoid fields, in particular showing that the perfect hull of $\mathbb{F}_p(t)^h$ is elementarily embedded in the perfect hull of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$. Recent work (e.g., the 2026 preprint "AKE principles for deeply ramified fields" and related theses) extends some results to deeply ramified fields of positive characteristic with fixed finite degree of imperfection. However, a full model-theoretic understanding of arbitrary (roughly) deeply ramified fields relative to value group and residue field remains open, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Beyond the Fontaine-Wintenberger theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Jahnke–Kartas prove AKE-type results for certain perfectoid/deeply ramified fields, including model-theoretic comparisons of perfect hulls of Fp(t)^h and Fp((t)).
status_evidence.claim: Partial results are known for the perfect deeply ramified case.

status_evidence.title: AKE principles for deeply ramified fields
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizes the perfect case treated by Jahnke and Kartas, obtaining Ax-Kochen/Ershov principles for certain deeply ramified fields of positive characteristic and fixed degree of imperfection.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial AKE results for deeply ramified fields beyond the perfect case.

status_evidence.title: Model theory of tame valued fields and beyond: open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as Open problem 5 the question of the model theory of (roughly) deeply ramified fields, in particular Fp((t))^{1/p^infty}.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem is explicitly recorded as open.
